### Summary

A conservation budget answers whether each conserved row changed only by what crossed the domain's boundary. The
budget consumer reads the register after each accepted step: the step field gives what crossed each boundary face,
and the state gives the totals. A budget output writes one record per interval to a NetCDF time series; the cycle
line printed every `ncycle_out` steps uses the same totals.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Per interval and row: the total, its change and the outward boundary transfer, which balance when no
source acts ([-@eq-ch10-budget-close]).

**Data.** FP64 sums on the CPU per record: totals, change, boundary, monitor counters and minima; written to
`<basename>.budget.nc`.

**Placement.** Observed after each accepted step; recorded at the output's cadence and on the final write.

**Activation.** `outputs: - {type: budget, dt: ...}`; off by default. The cycle line prints every `ncycle_out`
steps.

**Guarantee / limits.** Closes to round-off on a source-free run; the fixer, source and residual columns are not
written yet.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer of this section.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathbf Q$ is the vector of row totals, $\mathbf Q = \sum_i \mathbf U_i V_i$ over interior cells;
$\mathbf B$ is the outward boundary transfer of an interval, one value per row.

### Derivation

Integrate the conservation law $\partial_t\mathbf U + \nabla\cdot\mathbf F = 0$ over the fluid domain and over one
step. The finite-volume update changes $\mathbf Q$ only through the face fluxes, and interior faces cancel in
pairs, so the change of $\mathbf Q$ over a step is minus the time-integrated flux through the boundary faces. The
step field of @sec-ch10-amounts is exactly that time integral per face, $\mathbf S_d$, so with outward signs
$\sigma_f = \pm 1$

$$
\mathbf B = \sum_{\text{steps}}\ \sum_{f \in \partial\Omega} \sigma_f A_f\,\mathbf S_d[f], \qquad
\mathbf Q^{\mathrm{end}} - \mathbf Q^{\mathrm{start}} + \mathbf B = 0
$$ {#eq-ch10-budget-close}

The boundary sum is {{< code src/diagnostics/budget.cpp BudgetConsumer::boundary >}}.

up to round-off, when no cell source, floor or fixer changes a row. The boundary faces are the block faces with a
physical boundary condition that is not periodic, whose interior cell is fluid, and the faces of an immersed solid
with one solid neighbour, outward from the fluid; interior, seam, panel and periodic faces are never counted.

### Numerical method

`observe` runs in the acceptance branch of each step: it adds the step's boundary transfer, the monitor's counters
and minima to the block's pending sums and the step length to the interval. The face weights $\sigma_f A_f$ are built
once. An interval starts at a record, from a restart's carry, or, with neither, at the first observe, whose own step
then stays out. A record closes the interval: each local block's part is summed in block order, then over the
processes, and the root appends the record to the series. A restart stores the open interval's sums, so the
resumed run's next record equals the uninterrupted run's. The cycle line takes its conserved totals from the same
function, in the same summation order, and reads the kinetic and potential energy and the meters from the hydro
module (@fig-ch10-cycle-line).

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch10-cycle-line
#| fig-cap: "One cycle line, token by token: what each token sums over interior cells and local blocks, and how it is reduced to the root process. The conserved totals come from the budget's totals; the meters below the line are run-to-date values read from the hydro module."
#| fig-alt: "A table of nine tokens of the cycle line; each row gives the token, the volume integral or meter it prints, and the reduction (sum, minimum or maximum) used across blocks and processes."
#| echo: false
```

: The code of budgets and the cycle line. {#tbl-ch10-budget-code}

Walk-through: `apply_redo`, when no cause is set, calls each output's `observe` with the step length; a budget
output passes it to its consumer. `write_output_file` closes the block's interval and, when the last local block of
the process has recorded, reduces and appends. A build without NetCDF stops at the first record with an error that
names `NETCDF=ON`.

### Limits

The record has no fixer, source or residual column: those need the register's cell amounts and come with a later
step, so a run with cell sources does not close on the boundary column alone. With the default face-flux covariance
on, the covariance's energy increment does not reach the register's boundary faces, so the energy row of an outflow
run does not close on the boundary column alone; the closure test turns the covariance off, and how much the energy
row then misses is not measured at the pin (missing evidence). Two Meshes of one process that write the same
`basename` share one series file. Switch combinations are in @sec-ch12-matrix; the restart file's contents are in
@sec-ch14-restart.
